clue.text: Gum-chewing cricket side living together as brothers

indicators.note: the gum chews, holding something in its mouth, so it wraps around the cricket side

parts.note: mastic is a resin used as a gum
on is the leg side of the field in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket team chomps gum as they live together like a band of brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' puts ON inside MASTIC. ON (the on side, also called leg side) is one half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks live communally as a brotherhood, and monastic describes that way of life.

clue.text: Light work performed at the Savoy?

definitions.text: Light work performed at the Savoy?

parts.words: Light work performed at the Savoy?
parts.note: the Savoy Theatre in London staged the comic Gilbert and Sullivan pieces, light musical works

explanation.surface: A gentle show staged at a famous London venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light work' sounds like easy labour, but it means light music theatre; the Savoy Theatre was built for Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic opera with spoken dialogue is light musical work of the kind Gilbert and Sullivan wrote.

clue.text: Concerned with R3?

parts.note: the three Rs of basic schooling are reading, writing and reckoning with numbers; R3 suggests a power or calculation

explanation.surface: Something to do with a radio station or a mathematical cube.
explanation.walkthrough: R3 looks like Radio 3 or R cubed, a sum; it is read as the three Rs, the basics of schooling, the last of which is the numerical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes dealing with sums and numbers, the third of the three Rs.

clue.text: Unorthodox patterns of church wing

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange designs decorating part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The crosswise arm of a cross-shaped church building forms its wings.

clue.text: That free-French bore!

parts.note: ça is French for that
libre is French for free

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a tedious Free French officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free French' evokes de Gaulle's wartime forces, but 'French' tells you to translate: 'that free' becomes ça libre in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The bore of a gun is its internal diameter, also called its gauge.

clue.text: Priest from the Magic Circle

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters of the next word are conjured into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman who belongs to the famous society of conjurors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a London society of stage magicians; here 'Magic' rearranges CIRCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the clergy, such as a priest, is a churchman.

clue.text: Salmon in best possible condition

explanation.surface: A fish that is in fine fettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salmon' looks like the fish but is the colour; 'in the pink' means in perfect health.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon is a pale reddish shade; the phrase 'the pink of condition' means the very peak of health.

clue.text: Gives special prominence to films

explanation.surface: A cinema programme spotlights certain movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine that highlights something gives it a spotlight; full-length movies are called feature films.

clue.text: Comprehensive relish made from pimento berries

parts.note: all means comprehensive, covering everything
spice means relish or zest, a flavouring

explanation.surface: A thorough sauce made with Jamaican berries.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice from dried Jamaican pimento berries tastes of several spices combined.

clue.text: Residence in Kent area, adjacent to main road

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, abbreviated SE
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A house in Kent close to a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; the digit 1 is read as the letter I. Kent is a county in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house, shortened, is a common British home.

clue.text: Equipment causing disturbance in court?'

parts.note: a racket is a din, and a court can be one where a ball game is played rather than a law court

explanation.surface: Something that causes a commotion during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a courtroom and 'disturbance' a row; read as the sports court and a racket (both a din and the bat), it is sporting kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The strung bat used on a lawn or hard court in that game is this item of sports kit.

clue.text: Like a full union member's eccentric bearing

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
bearing means carrying, holding up

explanation.surface: A trade unionist's odd posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is the old sense of an eccentric character.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully paid-up union member holds a membership card, so they are a registered, committed member.

clue.text: Your head stuck in tricky Times puzzle?

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside the jumbled letters of the newspaper's name
tricky signals the letters of the next word are twisted into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Is the newspaper's crossword a teaser for your brain?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges TIMES to STMIE; 'stuck in' puts Y, the head of 'Your', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie someone is to baffle or thwart them, much as a puzzle does.

clue.text: Judge of a fipple flute

explanation.surface: A judge who plays a simple wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a recorder is a part-time judge in the Crown Court. A fipple is the block that forms the mouthpiece of a whistle-type flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time British criminal court judge holds this title; the school woodwind with a blocked mouthpiece is the same word.

clue.text: Tin soldiers augmented for this musical work

parts.note: a can is a tin container

indicators.note: augmented means increased, so the soldiers are doubled up here

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Toy soldiers enlarged for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin soldiers' looks like toys; split it as can plus TA, the Territorial Army, and 'augmented' doubles TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition with soloists and orchestra is a sung piece of music.

clue.text: Thriller-writer whose subjects are snuffed out?

explanation.surface: An author of crime novels whose characters get killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote the Philip Marlowe thrillers; a chandler makes candles, which get snuffed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote hardboiled detective stories; a maker of candles makes wicks that are extinguished.

clue.text: Body of accountants found in saloons

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the saloons

parts.note: saloons are cars with closed bodies
CA is a chartered accountant, so CAS are accountants

explanation.surface: A group of accountants turns up in some bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloons' looks like bars, but saloon is the British word for a sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead animal's corpse is its body, or a framework or shell.

clue.text: Lad hopes to cultivate Lily

indicators.note: to cultivate is to work the soil, so these letters are dug over into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy hopes to grow a flower called Lily.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Lily' makes it look like a girl's name; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a plant of the lily family, a flower of Greek myth.

clue.text: Remitted about ten cents in settlement

indicators.note: about means going around, so the posted word encloses the coin

parts.note: remitted means sent, of money
a dime is a US coin worth ten cents

explanation.surface: Money paid towards a financial settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' suggests a payment, but it means matter settling at the bottom of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles to the bottom of a liquid forms a deposit.

clue.text: Must this cavalryman be sworn in?

definitions.text: Must this cavalryman be sworn in?

parts.words: Must this cavalryman be sworn in?
parts.note: being sworn in suggests an oath of enlistment, but the idiom about swearing like a mounted soldier means cursing heavily

explanation.surface: Does this horse soldier have to take an oath on joining up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'sworn in' looks like enlistment, but the phrase 'swear like a trooper' means to curse a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry soldier of private rank is called by this name.

clue.text: Power-seat, source of much criticism

parts.note: arm means power, as in the strong arm of the law
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A powerful seat from which criticism comes.
explanation.walkthrough: An armchair critic judges from comfort, without first-hand experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Commentators who judge from home are called critics from the easy chair, a phrase for second-hand censure.

clue.text: Mysterious interior of quasar can explode

indicators.note: interior of means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The mysterious core of a distant galaxy may blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arcane is secret, understood by only a few.

clue.text: Staff earnings outside to take off

indicators.note: outside means the earnings wrap around the staff

parts.note: pay is earnings
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Workers' wages are cut to remove them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick; 'take off' means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone comically, imitating their manner, is to send them up.

clue.text: Salad of cole got daily in Higgins' study. .

indicators.note: a salad is a mixed jumble, so these letters are tossed together

explanation.surface: A coleslaw eaten every day during a professor's research.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Higgins is the phonetics professor in Shaw's Pygmalion, who studies regional speech; cole is cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of regional forms of speech was Professor Higgins's speciality in the play.

clue.text: Book works

explanation.surface: A volume of writings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Testament volume has this name; deeds or doings are also this.

clue.text: … I protest endlessly, getting the same

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the protest is dropped

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: I keep complaining and get the same response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final O from DEMO, a short form of demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for 'the same', used in references to an author already cited.

clue.text: Is classical course cut off?

parts.note: est is Latin for is, and Latin is the classical language
a range is a course or sweep, as of hills or of options

explanation.surface: Is a traditional school subject being dropped?
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical' tells you to put 'Is' into Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to sever a bond with them, as with relatives.

clue.text: Soldiers have messenger put down

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a legate is an envoy or messenger, as of the Pope

explanation.surface: Troops are given a courier to be put down.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote someone is to put them down to a lower rank or division.
